objects.description: Built-in type; no custom types are defined in this header. Note: This entry is included only to clarify that there are no user-defined structs, enums, typedefs, or classes present. All declarations use built-in C types (long, double, char) and function prototypes only.

functions.name: Set_UTM_Parameters
functions.signature: long Set_UTM_Parameters(double a, double f, long override);
functions.description: Sets the global/state UTM configuration using the provided ellipsoid parameters and an optional UTM zone override. Returns a bitwise-OR combination of error codes on invalid inputs, or UTM_NO_ERROR (0) on success. Typical usage: call once to configure the ellipsoid (semi-major axis and flattening) and optionally force a specific UTM zone before performing conversions.
requirements: a (semi-major axis) must be greater than 0 meters; otherwise UTM_A_ERROR may be returned.
f (flattening) must represent a valid ellipsoid flattening such that the inverse flattening (1/f) lies within 250 to 350; otherwise UTM_INV_F_ERROR may be returned.

override is the UTM zone override: 0 indicates no override; if non-zero, it should be an integer in the range [1, 60]. Values outside [1,60] can trigger UTM_ZONE_ERROR or UTM_ZONE_OVERRIDE_ERROR (the latter applies when outside [1,60] but within 1 of the 'natural' zone).
Caller must check the return value for non-zero to detect errors (bitwise-OR of UTM_* error flags).
Function relies on internal state; subsequent conversions use the parameters set by this call.

functions.name: Get_UTM_Parameters
functions.signature: void Get_UTM_Parameters(double *a, double *f, long *override);
functions.description: Retrieves the current ellipsoid parameters and the UTM zone override previously set by Set_UTM_Parameters. Intended for inspection or serialization of the current UTM configuration.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to receive the semi-major axis in meters.
f must be a non-null pointer to receive the flattening value.
override must be a non-null pointer to receive the current UTM zone override (0 if none).
Call only after the library has been initialized to a known state (either defaults or via Set_UTM_Parameters); exact defaults are not documented.

functions.name: Convert_Geodetic_To_UTM
functions.signature: long Convert_Geodetic_To_UTM(double Latitude, double Longitude, long *Zone, char *Hemisphere, double *Easting, double *Northing);
functions.description: Converts geodetic coordinates (latitude, longitude in radians) to UTM coordinates (zone, hemisphere, easting, northing) using the current ellipsoid parameters and any configured UTM zone override. Returns UTM_NO_ERROR on success, or a bitwise-OR of UTM_* error codes if inputs are out of range.
requirements: Latitude is in radians; valid range corresponds to -80.5 to 84.5 degrees (approximately -1.405 to 1.475 radians). Out-of-range latitudes produce UTM_LAT_ERROR.
Longitude is in radians; valid range corresponds to -180 to 360 degrees (approximately -π to 2π radians). Out-of-range longitudes produce UTM_LON_ERROR.
Zone must be a non-null pointer to receive the computed UTM zone (1–60), unless a zone override is active.
Hemisphere must be a non-null pointer to receive 'N' or 'S'. Invalid hemisphere values are reported via UTM_HEMISPHERE_ERROR when applicable.
Easting must be a non-null pointer to receive easting in meters; valid easting range is 100,000 to 900,000 meters. If results fall outside, UTM_EASTING_ERROR may be reported.
Northing must be a non-null pointer to receive northing in meters; valid northing range is 0 to 10,000,000 meters. If results fall outside, UTM_NORTHING_ERROR may be reported.
Caller must check the return value; non-zero indicates one or more error flags (bitwise-OR).
Uses parameters set by Set_UTM_Parameters; if not set, implementation-defined defaults apply (not documented).

functions.name: Convert_UTM_To_Geodetic
functions.signature: long Convert_UTM_To_Geodetic(long Zone, char Hemisphere, double Easting, double Northing, double *Latitude, double *Longitude);
functions.description: Converts UTM coordinates (zone, hemisphere, easting, northing) to geodetic latitude/longitude (in radians) using the current ellipsoid parameters. Returns UTM_NO_ERROR on success, or a bitwise-OR of UTM_* error codes on invalid inputs.
requirements: Zone must be an integer in the inclusive range [1, 60]; otherwise UTM_ZONE_ERROR may be returned.
Hemisphere must be either 'N' or 'S'; otherwise UTM_HEMISPHERE_ERROR may be returned.
Easting must be within [100000, 900000] meters; otherwise UTM_EASTING_ERROR may be returned.
Northing must be within [0, 10000000] meters; otherwise UTM_NORTHING_ERROR may be returned.
Latitude must be a non-null pointer to receive the latitude in radians.
Longitude must be a non-null pointer to receive the longitude in radians.
Caller must check the return value; non-zero indicates one or more error flags (bitwise-OR).
Uses parameters set by Set_UTM_Parameters; if not set, implementation-defined defaults apply (not documented).

functions.name: Set_USNG_Parameters
functions.description: Sets global/state ellipsoid parameters used by all USNG conversions. Call this before performing conversions that depend on the ellipsoid. Returns a bitwise-ORed error code or USNG_NO_ERROR on success. Intended usage: provide semi-major axis (meters), flattening, and a 2-letter ellipsoid code.
requirements: a (semi-major axis) must be > 0; otherwise USNG_A_ERROR may be returned.

Flattening f must be valid; implementation signals USNG_INV_F_ERROR when inverse flattening is outside [250,350]. As f is flattening, it should correspond to an inverse flattening in [250,350] (i.e., roughly f in (1/350, 1/250]); exact check is implementation-defined.
Ellipsoid_Code must point to a valid, writable/readable C string containing a 2-letter ellipsoid code (input). Unknown accepted codes; invalid codes may contribute to an error code (unspecified).
Function may combine multiple error codes using bitwise OR; caller must check the return value against USNG_NO_ERROR (0).
May set internal state used by subsequent conversions; should be called before conversion functions if defaults are not desired.

functions.name: Get_USNG_Parameters
functions.description: Retrieves the current ellipsoid parameters previously set (or defaults). Populates the provided outputs with semi-major axis (meters), flattening, and a 2-letter ellipsoid code.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to receive the semi-major axis (output).
f must be a non-null pointer to receive the flattening (output).
Ellipsoid_Code must be a non-null pointer to writable memory sufficient to hold the 2-letter code plus terminator (exact size not specified; ensure at least 3 bytes).

functions.name: Convert_Geodetic_To_USNG
functions.signature:
long Convert_Geodetic_To_USNG (double Latitude,
                                 double Longitude,
                                 long   Precision,
                                 char *USNG);
functions.description: Converts geodetic latitude/longitude (in radians) to a USNG coordinate string using the current ellipsoid parameters. Returns a bitwise-ORed status code or USNG_NO_ERROR on success; writes the USNG string to the provided buffer.
requirements: Latitude is in radians and must be within valid geodetic limits equivalent to [-90, 90] degrees (i.e., approximately [-π/2, π/2]); otherwise USNG_LAT_ERROR may be returned.
Longitude is in radians and must be within valid limits equivalent to [-180, 360] degrees (i.e., approximately [-π, 2π]); otherwise USNG_LON_ERROR may be returned.

USNG must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer large enough to hold the resulting USNG string plus null terminator; required maximum length is not specified in this header (caller must provide sufficient space).
Ellipsoid parameters should be set appropriately beforehand via Set_USNG_Parameters if defaults are not desired.
Multiple error conditions may be ORed in the return value; caller must compare against USNG_NO_ERROR (0).

functions.name: Set_Transverse_Mercator_Parameters
functions.signature: long Set_Transverse_Mercator_Parameters(double a, double f, double Origin_Latitude, double Central_Meridian, double False_Easting, double False_Northing, double Scale_Factor);
functions.description: Initializes the module’s ellipsoid and Transverse Mercator projection parameters. Must be called before performing conversions. Returns a bitwise-ORed error/status code; TRANMERC_NO_ERROR indicates success. Error codes report invalid parameter ranges; a longitude-distance warning may be reported in later conversions if the central meridian is far from queried longitudes.
requirements: a (semi-major axis) must be > 0 meters (TRANMERC_A_ERROR otherwise).
f (flattening) must be such that the inverse flattening 1/f is within [250, 350] (TRANMERC_INV_F_ERROR otherwise).
Origin_Latitude must be within [-90, 90] degrees (i.e., [-π/2, π/2] radians) (TRANMERC_ORIGIN_LAT_ERROR otherwise).
Central_Meridian must be within [-180, 360] degrees (i.e., [-π, 2π] radians) (TRANMERC_CENT_MER_ERROR otherwise).
Scale_Factor must be within [0.3, 3.0] (TRANMERC_SCALE_FACTOR_ERROR otherwise).
Units: angular inputs are in radians; linear inputs/outputs in meters, as documented.
False_Easting and False_Northing are accepted in meters; no explicit numeric bounds documented.
Caller must check the returned long bitmask for errors; TRANMERC_NO_ERROR means success; multiple errors may be ORed.

functions.name: Get_Transverse_Mercator_Parameters
functions.signature: void Get_Transverse_Mercator_Parameters(double *a, double *f, double *Origin_Latitude, double *Central_Meridian, double *False_Easting, double *False_Northing, double *Scale_Factor);
functions.description: Retrieves the current ellipsoid and Transverse Mercator projection parameters previously set in the module. Outputs are written through the provided pointers.
requirements: All output pointers (a, f, Origin_Latitude, Central_Meridian, False_Easting, False_Northing, Scale_Factor) must be non-null and writable.
Parameters are returned in the same units used by the setter: a in meters; f as flattening; angles in radians; false easting/northing in meters; scale factor unitless.
Should be called after Set_Transverse_Mercator_Parameters has initialized the module; default/uninitialized state is not documented.

functions.name: Convert_Geodetic_To_Transverse_Mercator
functions.signature: long Convert_Geodetic_To_Transverse_Mercator(double Latitude, double Longitude, double *Easting, double *Northing);
functions.description: Converts geodetic coordinates (latitude, longitude) in radians to Transverse Mercator projection coordinates (easting, northing) in meters using the current ellipsoid and projection parameters. Returns a bitwise-ORed status; TRANMERC_NO_ERROR indicates success. May also return TRANMERC_LON_WARNING when longitude is far from the central meridian.
requirements: Set_Transverse_Mercator_Parameters must have been successfully called beforehand to establish ellipsoid and projection parameters.
Latitude must be within [-90, 90] degrees ([-π/2, π/2] radians) or TRANMERC_LAT_ERROR is returned.
Longitude must be within [-180, 360] degrees ([-π, 2π] radians) and within ±90 degrees (±π/2 radians) of the current Central Meridian; otherwise TRANMERC_LON_ERROR is returned.
If the input longitude is more than 9 degrees from the Central Meridian, TRANMERC_LON_WARNING may be ORed in the return code (distortion warning).
Easting and Northing output pointers must be non-null and writable.

On success, Easting and Northing are returned in meters; if projected values fall outside valid ranges (dependent on ellipsoid/projection), TRANMERC_EASTING_ERROR and/or TRANMERC_NORTHING_ERROR may be set.
Caller must inspect the returned long bitmask; multiple error bits may be ORed.

functions.name: Convert_Transverse_Mercator_To_Geodetic
functions.signature: long Convert_Transverse_Mercator_To_Geodetic(double Easting, double Northing, double *Latitude, double *Longitude);
functions.description: Converts Transverse Mercator projection coordinates (easting, northing) in meters to geodetic coordinates (latitude, longitude) in radians using the current ellipsoid and projection parameters. Returns a bitwise-ORed status; TRANMERC_NO_ERROR indicates success.
requirements: Set_Transverse_Mercator_Parameters must have been successfully called beforehand to establish ellipsoid and projection parameters.

Easting and Northing inputs must be within valid ranges for the current ellipsoid and projection setup; otherwise TRANMERC_EASTING_ERROR and/or TRANMERC_NORTHING_ERROR may be set. Specific numeric bounds are not documented and depend on parameters.
Latitude and Longitude output pointers must be non-null and writable.

On success, Latitude and Longitude are returned in radians; if results imply latitude outside [-π/2, π/2] or longitude outside [-π, 2π] or outside ±π/2 of the central meridian, corresponding LAT/LON error codes may be set as documented for range checks.
Caller must inspect the returned long bitmask; multiple error bits may be ORed.

functions.name: Set_UPS_Parameters
functions.signature: long Set_UPS_Parameters(double a, double f);
functions.description: Sets the current ellipsoid parameters used by all subsequent UPS conversions. Returns a bitwise-OR of error codes if validation fails, otherwise UPS_NO_ERROR (0). Intended to be called at initialization or whenever switching ellipsoids.
requirements: a (semi-major axis) must be greater than 0 meters; otherwise UPS_A_ERROR is set.

The ellipsoid inverse flattening (1/f) must be within [250, 350]; otherwise UPS_INV_F_ERROR is set. If f = 0 (sphere), behavior is unknown; header only documents inverse flattening bounds via UPS_INV_F_ERROR.
Caller should check the returned long for non-zero error codes; multiple errors may be ORed together.
May be called before any Convert_* function to use non-default ellipsoid parameters; subsequent conversions use the parameters set here.
Thread-safety and global state behavior are unknown (the function sets internal state).

functions.name: Convert_Geodetic_To_UPS
functions.signature: long Convert_Geodetic_To_UPS(double Latitude, double Longitude, char *Hemisphere, double *Easting, double *Northing);
functions.description: Converts geodetic coordinates (latitude, longitude in radians) to UPS coordinates (hemisphere, easting, northing) using the current ellipsoid parameters. On invalid input, returns a bitwise-OR of error codes; otherwise UPS_NO_ERROR and fills outputs.
requirements: Latitude is in radians and must lie within UPS-valid polar bands: North Pole 83.5° to 90° (≈ 1.457349 to π/2 rad) or South Pole −90° to −79.5° (≈ −π/2 to −1.387537 rad); otherwise UPS_LAT_ERROR is set.
Longitude is in radians and must be within −180° to 360° (≈ −π to 2π rad); otherwise UPS_LON_ERROR is set.
Hemisphere must be a valid, non-null pointer; on success it is set to 'N' or 'S' based on the input latitude; behavior for null is unknown.
Easting must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the easting in meters; behavior for null is unknown.
Northing must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the northing in meters; behavior for null is unknown.
On success, output easting and northing are within [0, 4,000,000] meters; range violations would set UPS_EASTING_ERROR and/or UPS_NORTHING_ERROR if produced by computation.
Uses the current ellipsoid parameters (set via Set_UPS_Parameters or defaults).
Caller must check the returned long for non-zero error codes; multiple errors may be ORed together.

functions.name: Convert_UPS_To_Geodetic
functions.signature: long Convert_UPS_To_Geodetic(char Hemisphere, double Easting, double Northing, double *Latitude, double *Longitude);
functions.description: Converts UPS coordinates (hemisphere, easting, northing) to geodetic coordinates (latitude, longitude in radians) using the current ellipsoid parameters. Returns a bitwise-OR of error codes on invalid input; otherwise UPS_NO_ERROR and fills outputs.
requirements: Hemisphere must be either 'N' or 'S'; otherwise UPS_HEMISPHERE_ERROR is set.
Easting (meters) must be within [0, 4,000,000]; otherwise UPS_EASTING_ERROR is set.
Northing (meters) must be within [0, 4,000,000]; otherwise UPS_NORTHING_ERROR is set.
Latitude must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive latitude in radians; behavior for null is unknown.
Longitude must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive longitude in radians; behavior for null is unknown.
Resulting longitude nominal range is −180° to 360° (≈ −π to 2π rad); violations would set UPS_LON_ERROR if applicable by implementation.

functions.description: Initializes the internal ellipsoid and Polar Stereographic projection parameters used by subsequent conversions. Function returns error codes via its return value; callers must check the return for POLAR_NO_ERROR before proceeding.
Parameters set here define the state for later conversions and must be successfully set before calling any Convert_* functions.

data_types.description: A short ASCII string representing an ellipsoid identifier used by the USNG/MGRS/UTM library. Expected to be exactly two alphabetic characters (e.g., 'AA', 'WF'), stored as a null-terminated C string. Implementations may validate against a known set; malformed inputs can be any length or contain non-letters in fuzzing contexts.

A text string encoding a United States National Grid (USNG) coordinate. Typical forms include zone number (1–60) and latitude band letter, followed by 100 km grid square letters and an even number of numeric digits for easting/northing at precisions 0–5 (e.g., '18S UJ 23480 06470', '32U MR 12345 67890', or compact forms without spaces). Input is a null-terminated ASCII string; parser should handle varying whitespace and case.

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets the Set_USNG_Parameters fuzzer stub.
# The only FUZZ_PARAM_STR used there is to occasionally supply a malformed/variant
# Ellipsoid_Code. We therefore produce a bytes buffer that primarily contains
# useful 2-letter ellipsoid codes (null-terminated C strings) and, at times,
# deliberately varied strings (different lengths, embedded NULs, non-ASCII) while
# ensuring overall input remains valid as a byte buffer. The fuzzer framework
# will slice from this buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and possibly other FUZZ_PARAM calls.
# We keep the overall buffer <= 4096 bytes.

# A small set of realistic 2-letter ellipsoid codes commonly seen in mapping libs
# (note: actual accepted set is implementation-dependent). We include common EPSG/DoD-like codes
# used historically in USNG/MGRS contexts to increase chance of acceptance.
REALISTIC_CODES = [
    b"WE",  # WGS84 (placeholder two-letter form)
    b"WF",  # WGS72
    b"AN",  # Airy 1830 (nominal)
    b"AA",  # Australian National
    b"KA",  # Krasovsky 1940
    b"IN",  # International 1924
    b"CL",  # Clarke 1866/1880 (placeholder)
    b"GR",  # GRS80
    b"HE",  # Helmert 1906
    b"FA",  # GRS67 (fallback)
]

# Some interesting malformed variants to exercise error paths in code validation
# while still being valid C strings when interpreted.
MALFORMED_VARIANTS = [
    b"",                      # empty
    b"A",                     # single char
    b"ABC",                   # 3 chars
    b"A1",                    # alnum
    b"1A",                    # starts with digit
    b"@@",                    # punctuation
    b"we",                    # lowercase
    b"W\x00F",               # embedded NUL inside
    b"LONGCODE",              # long (>2)
    b" \t",                   # whitespace
]

# Random helper: weighted choice

def wchoice(rng: random.Random, items: List, weights: List[float]):
    total = sum(weights)
    x = rng.random() * total
    acc = 0.0
    for item, w in zip(items, weights):
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return item
    return items[-1]

# Build a single C-string (null-terminated) blob

def cstr(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure there is exactly one terminating NUL at end; any internal NULs remain
    if data.endswith(b"\x00"):
        return data
    return data + b"\x00"

# Construct a corpus of candidate strings mixing valid and edge cases.

def build_ellipsoid_strings(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> List[bytes]:
    out: List[bytes] = []

    # Seed with a few guaranteed good two-letter uppercase codes
    good_pool = REALISTIC_CODES.copy()

    # Generate additional random good codes
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)):
        c1 = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        c2 = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
        good_pool.append((c1 + c2).encode('ascii'))

    # Some malformed strings, possibly with random lengths
    bad_pool = MALFORMED_VARIANTS.copy()

    # Add a few random-length strings (1..16), possibly including lowercase, digits, punctuation
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .:@#"
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)):
        L = rng.randint(1, 16)
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(L)).encode('ascii')
        bad_pool.append(s)

    # Also add some with high-bit bytes (non-ASCII) to check handling
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        L = rng.randint(2, 8)
        b = bytes(rng.randint(0, 255) for _ in range(L))
        bad_pool.append(b)

    # Mix them with weights: mostly valid, some invalid
    # The stub uses malformed only ~10% of the time, but FUZZ framework may reuse strings broadly.
    while sum(len(s) + 1 for s in out) < budget and len(out) < 128:
        pick = wchoice(rng, ["good", "bad"], [0.7, 0.3])
        if pick == "good":
            out.append(cstr(rng.choice(good_pool)))
        else:
            out.append(cstr(rng.choice(bad_pool)))

    return out

# We also include some doubles/ints encoded to help FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int/double)
# pull useful values from the same buffer in some harnesses. While FUZZ_PARAM_* in
# this environment is independent, embedding canonical doubles can still be useful
# if the fuzzer maps reads sequentially.

def pack_double(x: float) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<d', x)

def pack_uint(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

# Build a header of numeric seeds likely to produce valid flattening and semi-major axis

def build_numeric_header(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    buf = bytearray()
    # a: semi-major axis candidates (meters)
    for a in [6378137.0, 6378135.0, 6378206.4, 6378245.0]:
        buf += pack_double(a)
    # f: flattening values around common ellipsoids
    for f in [1/298.257223563, 1/297.0, 1/300.0, 1/350.0, 1/250.0]:
        buf += pack_double(f)
    # Some unsigned ints to influence inv_candidate (250..350) and flip flags
    for u in [250, 298, 300, 349, 350, 0, 1, 2, 10, 11, 20, 21]:
        buf += pack_uint(u)
    # Random extras
    for _ in range(8):
        buf += pack_uint(rng.randrange(0, 2**32))
    return bytes(buf)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Budget: keep total <= 4096
    max_size = 4096

    # Start with numeric header
    buf = bytearray()
    buf += build_numeric_header(rng)

    # Build a series of C-strings for Ellipsoid_Code candidates
    # Reserve space: leave at least 512 bytes slack
    remaining = max_size - len(buf) - 512
    remaining = max(256, remaining)  # ensure some capacity for strings

    strings = build_ellipsoid_strings(rng, remaining)

    # Prepend a few highly-likely-valid two-letter codes first
    prime = [cstr(code) for code in REALISTIC_CODES[:5]]
    payload = b"".join(prime + strings)

    # If still too large, truncate payload at a NUL boundary
    if len(buf) + len(payload) > max_size:
        # Find last NUL within limit
        limit = max_size - len(buf)
        cut = payload.rfind(b"\x00", 0, limit)
        if cut == -1:
            payload = payload[:limit]
        else:
            payload = payload[:cut+1]

    buf += payload

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import math
from typing import List, Tuple

# USNG generator for valid, interesting inputs.
# We focus on producing syntactically correct USNG strings across zones, bands, grid squares,
# and varying precisions, including compact and spaced forms, mixed case, and polar UPS forms.

# Constants and helpers derived from USNG/MGRS conventions

# Latitude bands (C..X excluding I,O); X extends to 84N; C starts at -80S
LATITUDE_BANDS = [
    ('C', -80), ('D', -72), ('E', -64), ('F', -56), ('G', -48), ('H', -40),
    ('J', -32), ('K', -24), ('L', -16), ('M', -8), ('N', 0), ('P', 8), ('Q', 16),
    ('R', 24), ('S', 32), ('T', 40), ('U', 48), ('V', 56), ('W', 64), ('X', 72)
]

# 100km grid square column letters by zone banding pattern (A..Z without I,O)
# Easting columns repeat every 3 zones with sets:
# 1,4,7,... use: A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z
# 2,5,8,... use: J K L M N P Q R S T U V W X Y Z A B C D E F G H
# 3,6,9,... use: S T U V W X Y Z A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R
COL_SETS = [
    "ABCDEFGHJKLmnopqrstuvwxyz".upper().replace('O','').replace('I',''),
    "JKLmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGH".upper().replace('O','').replace('I',''),
    "STUVWXYZABCDEFGHJKLMNPQR"
]
# Normalize first two sets explicitly to avoid accidental replacements
COL_SETS[0] = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ"
COL_SETS[1] = "JKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZABCDEFGH"

# Northing row letters cycle every 2,000,000 m: A..Z without I,O; rows shift by zone odd/even
ROW_SET = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXZY"  # We'll correct with a canonical set below
# Correct canonical row set for 100km rows per MGRS: A..V excluding I,O (20 letters), then wraps
ROW_SET = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUV"

# Polar UPS grid designators for USNG (simplified typical sets)
# UPS uses bands A/B (south) and Y/Z (north) for USNG; grid letters vary by quadrant.
UPS_BANDS_N = ['Y', 'Z']
UPS_BANDS_S = ['A', 'B']
# Representative 100km grid letters for UPS quadrants (not exhaustive, but valid-looking)
UPS_GRIDS_N = ["ZS", "ZT", "ZU", "ZV", "YN", "YP", "YQ", "YR"]
UPS_GRIDS_S = ["AA", "AB", "AC", "AD", "BA", "BB", "BC", "BD"]

DIGITS = "0123456789"

def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str] | str):
    return seq[rng.randrange(0, len(seq))]

def pick_zone_and_band(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[int, str]:
    zone = rng.randint(1, 60)
    band = rand_choice(rng, LATITUDE_BANDS)[0]
    return zone, band

def grid_column_for_zone(rng: random.Random, zone: int) -> str:
    # Column letters depend on zone modulo 3
    idx = (zone - 1) % 3
    cols = COL_SETS[idx]
    return rand_choice(rng, cols)

def grid_row_for_zone(rng: random.Random, zone: int) -> str:
    # Row set advances with zone parity; odd zones start at A, even zones start at F (typical MGRS rule)
    # We'll select any valid row letter from A..V and rely on converter tolerance
    return rand_choice(rng, ROW_SET)

def pick_precision(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Bias towards common precisions but include full range 0..5
    weights = [1, 2, 4, 4, 3, 2]  # 0..5
    population = [0,1,2,3,4,5]
    choice_pool = []
    for p, w in zip(population, weights):
        choice_pool.extend([p]*w)
    return rand_choice(rng, choice_pool)

def make_easting_northing_digits(rng: random.Random, precision: int) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    if precision == 0:
        return "", ""
    # Each of easting/northing has 'precision' digits
    # Prefer mid-range values to avoid edge errors, but include extremes sometimes
    def mk(prec: int) -> str:
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            # edge-ish values
            v = rng.choice([0, 1, 8, 9])
            return str(v) * prec
        # mid-range
        return ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(prec))
    return mk(precision), mk(precision)

def maybe_compact_or_spaced(rng: random.Random, parts: List[str]) -> str:
    # Produce variants: normal spaced, compact, mixed spacing
    style = rng.random()
    if style < 0.3:
        # compact: no spaces
        return ''.join(parts)
    elif style < 0.6:
        # single spaces
        return ' '.join(filter(lambda s: len(s) > 0, parts))
    else:
        # mixed spaces and optional extra whitespace
        sep1 = ' ' * rng.randint(1, 3)
        sep2 = ' ' * rng.randint(1, 3)
        sep3 = ' ' * rng.randint(1, 3)
        seq = []
        for p in parts:
            if not p:
                continue
            if seq:
                seq.append(rand_choice(rng, [sep1, sep2, sep3]))
            seq.append(p)
        return ''.join(seq)

def maybe_mixed_case(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return s
    # randomly toggle case on letters
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isalpha():
            out.append(ch.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower())
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return ''.join(out)

def generate_utm_usng(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    zone, band = pick_zone_and_band(rng)
    col = grid_column_for_zone(rng, zone)
    row = grid_row_for_zone(rng, zone)
    precision = pick_precision(rng)
    e, n = make_easting_northing_digits(rng, precision)
    # Build parts; common forms: "32U MR 12345 67890" or compact "32UMR1234567890"
    parts = [str(zone) + band, col + row, e, n]
    s = maybe_compact_or_spaced(rng, parts)
    s = maybe_mixed_case(rng, s)
    return s

def generate_ups_usng(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # USNG for UPS typically omits zone number and uses band letter and 100km grid, then digits
    north = rng.random() < 0.5
    band = rand_choice(rng, UPS_BANDS_N if north else UPS_BANDS_S)
    grid = rand_choice(rng, UPS_GRIDS_N if north else UPS_GRIDS_S)
    precision = pick_precision(rng)
    e, n = make_easting_northing_digits(rng, precision)
    parts = [band, grid, e, n]
    s = maybe_compact_or_spaced(rng, parts)
    s = maybe_mixed_case(rng, s)
    return s

def generate_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create strings that are still valid-looking but stress boundaries
    choices = []
    # Minimal precision (0): e.g., "31T DQ"
    zone, band = 31, 'T'
    col = 'D'
    row = 'Q'
    choices.append(maybe_compact_or_spaced(rng, [str(zone)+band, col+row]))
    # Max precision (5) near extremes
    zone = 60
    band = 'X'
    col = 'Z'
    row = 'V'
    e = '9'*5 if rng.random() < 0.5 else '0'*5
    n = '0'*5 if e[0] == '9' else '9'*5
    choices.append(maybe_compact_or_spaced(rng, [str(zone)+band, col+row, e, n]))
    # Compact no-space mid-precision
    zone = 1
    band = 'C'
    col = 'A'
    row = 'A'
    e = '1234'
    n = '5678'
    choices.append(f"{zone}{band}{col}{row}{e}{n}")
    # UPS edge with precision 5
    band = 'Z'
    grid = 'ZU'
    e = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(5))
    n = ''.join(rng.choice(DIGITS) for _ in range(5))
    choices.append(maybe_compact_or_spaced(rng, [band, grid, e, n]))
    return rand_choice(rng, choices)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide which family to generate
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.6:
        s = generate_utm_usng(rng)
    elif mode < 0.9:
        s = generate_ups_usng(rng)
    else:
        s = generate_edge_cases(rng)
    # Ensure reasonable maximum length and ASCII
    if len(s) > 128:
        s = s[:128]
    # Add trailing newline sometimes (parser should ignore whitespace)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = s + "\n"
    return s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
